title: What's Missing From LLM Chatbots: A Sense of Purpose
title_zh: 缺乏目的感的LLM聊天机器人

paragraphs.en: LLM-based chatbots’ capabilities have been advancing every month. These improvements are mostly measured by benchmarks like MMLU, HumanEval, and MATH (e.g. sonnet 3.5, gpt-4o). However, as these measures get more and more saturated, is user experience increasing in proportion to these scores? If we envision a future of human-AI collaboration rather than AI replacing humans, the current ways of measuring dialogue systems may be insufficient because they measure in a non-interactive fashion.
paragraphs.zh: 基于 LLM 的聊天机器人的能力每个月都在进步。 这些进步大多通过 MMLU、HumanEval 和 MATH 等基准来衡量（例如 sonnet 3.5、gpt-4o）。 然而，随着这些指标越来越趋于饱和，用户体验是否也在与这些分数成比例地提升？ 如果我们展望的是人类与人工智能协作而非人工智能取代人类的未来，那么当前衡量对话系统的方式可能是不够的，因为它们以非交互的方式进行衡量。

paragraphs.en: Purposeful dialogue refers to a multi-round user-chatbot conversation that centers around a goal or intention. The goal could range from a generic one like “harmless and helpful” to more specific roles like “travel planning agent”, “psycho-therapist” or “customer service bot.”
paragraphs.zh: 目的性对话指围绕某个目标或意图展开的多轮用户与聊天机器人之间的对话。 该目标既可以是像「无害且有用」这样的宽泛目标，也可以是更具体的角色，如「旅行规划智能体」「心理治疗师」或「客服机器人」。

paragraphs.en: Travel planning is a simple, illustrative example. Our preferences, fellow travelers’ preference, and all the complexities of real-world situations make transmitting all information in one pass way too costly. However, if multiple back-and-forth exchanges of information are allowed, only important information gets selectively exchanged. Negotiation theory offers an analogy of this—iterative bargaining yields better outcomes than a take-it-or-leave-it offer.
paragraphs.zh: 旅行规划是一个简单、用于说明问题的例子。 我们的偏好、同行旅行者的偏好，以及现实情境中的各种复杂性，使得一次性传递所有信息的成本过高。 然而，如果允许信息多次来回交换，那么只有重要信息会被有选择地传递。 谈判理论为此提供了一个类比——反复讨价还价比“要么接受要么放弃”的报价产生更好的结果。

paragraphs.en: In fact, sharing information is only one aspect of dialogue. In Terry Winograd’s words: “All language use can be thought of as a way of activating procedures within the hearer.” We can think of each utterance as a deliberate action that one party takes to alter the world model of the other. What if both parties have more complicated, even hidden goals? In this way, purposeful dialogue provides us with a way of formulating human-AI interactions as a collaborative game, where the goal of chatbot is to help humans achieve certain goals.
paragraphs.zh: 事实上，信息共享只是对话的一个方面。 用特里·温诺格拉德的话说：“所有语言的使用都可以被看作是激活听者内部程序的一种方式。”我们可以把每句话都视为一方为了改变另一方世界模型而采取的深思熟虑的行动。 如果双方都有更复杂的、甚至隐藏的目标呢？ 这样一来，有目的的对话为我们提供了一种将人机交互表述为协作博弈的方式，其中聊天机器人的目标是帮助人类实现特定的目标。

paragraphs.en: This might seem like an unnecessary complexity that is only a concern for academics. However, purposeful dialogue could be beneficial even for the most hard-nosed, product-oriented research direction like code generation. Existing coding benchmarks mostly measure performances in a one-pass generation setting; however, for AI to automate solving ordinary Github issues (like in SWE-bench ), it’s unlikely to be achieved by a single action—the AI needs to communicate back and forth with human software engineers to make sure it understands the correct requirements, ask for missing documentation and data, and even ask humans to give it a hand if needed. In a similar vein to pair programming , this could reduce the defects of code but without the burden of increasing man-hours.
paragraphs.zh: 这看起来似乎是一种不必要的复杂化，只是学术界才需要关心的问题。 然而，有目的的对话即使在最务实、以产品为导向的研究方向（如代码生成）中也可能是有益的。 现有的编程基准大多衡量一次性生成设定下的表现；然而，要让 AI 自动解决普通的 Github 问题（如 SWE-bench 中那样），这不太可能通过单个动作实现——AI 需要与人类软件工程师来回沟通，以确保它理解正确的需求，索取缺失的文档和数据，甚至在需要时请人类搭把手。 类似于结对编程，这可以减少代码缺陷，但又不必增加工时负担。

paragraphs.en: Moreover, with the introduction of turn-taking, many new possibilities can be unlocked. As interactions become long-term and memory is built, the chatbot can gradually update user profiles. It can also adapt to their preferences. Imagine a personal assistant (e.g., IVA , Siri ) that, through daily interaction, learns your preferences and intentions. It can read your resources of new information automatically (e.g., twitter, arxiv, Slack, NYT) and provide you with a morning news summary according to your preferences. It can draft emails for you and keep improving by learning from your edits.
paragraphs.zh: 此外，随着轮次交互的引入，许多新的可能性将得以解锁。 随着交互变得长期化并建立起记忆，聊天机器人可以逐步更新用户画像。 它还可以适应用户的偏好。 想象一个个人助手（例如 IVA、Siri），它通过日常互动学习你的偏好和意图。 它可以自动读取你的新信息来源（例如 Twitter、arXiv、Slack、NYT），并根据你的偏好为你提供晨间新闻摘要。 它可以为你起草电子邮件，并通过学习你的修改不断改进。

paragraphs.en: In a nutshell, meaningful interactions between people rarely begin with complete strangers and conclude in just one exchange. Humans naturally interact with each other through multi-round dialogues and adapt accordingly throughout the conversation. However, doesn’t that seem exactly the opposite of predicting the next token, which is the cornerstone of modern LLMs? Below, let’s take a look at the makings of dialogue systems.
paragraphs.zh: 简而言之，人与人之间有意义的互动很少始于完全的陌生人，并在仅仅一次交流中就结束。 人类自然而然地通过多轮对话相互交流，并在整个对话过程中相应地做出调整。 然而，这是否恰恰与预测下一个词元相反？而后者正是现代大语言模型的基石。 下面，我们来看看对话系统的构成要素。

sents.en: In a nutshell, meaningful interactions between people rarely begin with complete strangers and conclude in just one exchange.
sents.zh: 简而言之，人与人之间有意义的互动很少始于完全的陌生人，并在仅仅一次交流中就结束。

sents.en: Humans naturally interact with each other through multi-round dialogues and adapt accordingly throughout the conversation.
sents.zh: 人类自然而然地通过多轮对话相互交流，并在整个对话过程中相应地做出调整。

sents.en: However, doesn’t that seem exactly the opposite of predicting the next token, which is the cornerstone of modern LLMs?
sents.zh: 然而，这是否恰恰与预测下一个词元相反？而后者正是现代大语言模型的基石。

sents.en: Below, let’s take a look at the makings of dialogue systems.
sents.zh: 下面，我们来看看对话系统的构成要素。

paragraphs.en: Let's jump back to the 1970s, when Roger Schank introduced his "restaurant script" as a kind of dialogue system [1]. This script breaks down the typical restaurant experience into steps like entering, ordering, eating, and paying, each with specific scripted utterances. Back then, every piece of dialogue in these scenarios was carefully planned out, enabling AI systems to mimic realistic conversations. ELIZA, a Rogerian psychotherapist simulator, and PARRY, a system mimicking a paranoid individual, were two other early dialogue systems until the dawn of machine learning.
paragraphs.zh: 让我们回到20世纪70年代，当时Roger Schank提出了他的「餐厅脚本」，作为一种对话系统[1]。 这个脚本将典型的餐厅体验分解为进入、点餐、用餐和付款等步骤，每个步骤都有特定的预设台词。 在那个年代，这些场景中的每一段对话都是精心规划的，使AI系统能够模仿逼真的对话。 ELIZA是一个罗杰斯式心理治疗师模拟器，PARRY是一个模仿偏执狂个体的系统，在机器学习兴起之前，它们是另外两个早期的对话系统。

paragraphs.en: Compare this approach to the LLM-based dialogue system today, it seems mysterious how models trained to predict the next token could do anything at all with engaging in dialogues. Therefore, let’s take a close examination of how dialogue systems are made, with an emphasis on how the dialogue format comes into play:
paragraphs.zh: 将这种方法与当今基于大语言模型的对话系统相比较，那些通过训练来预测下一个词元的模型竟然能做出任何事情，而不仅仅是进行对话，这看起来十分神秘。 因此，让我们仔细考察一下对话系统是如何构建的，重点关注对话格式在其中所起的作用：

sents.en: Compare this approach to the LLM-based dialogue system today, it seems mysterious how models trained to predict the next token could do anything at all with engaging in dialogues.
sents.zh: 将这种方法与当今基于大语言模型的对话系统相比较，那些通过训练来预测下一个词元的模型竟然能做出任何事情，而不仅仅是进行对话，这看起来十分神秘。

sents.en: Therefore, let’s take a close examination of how dialogue systems are made, with an emphasis on how the dialogue format comes into play:
sents.zh: 因此，让我们仔细考察一下对话系统是如何构建的，重点关注对话格式在其中所起的作用：

paragraphs.en: (1) Pretraining: a sequence model is trained to predict the next token on a gigantic corpus of mixed internet texts. The compositions may vary but they are predominantly news, books, Github code, with a small blend of forum-crawled data such as from Reddit, Stack Exchange, which may contain dialogue-like data.
paragraphs.zh: (1) 预训练：在一个由混合互联网文本组成的超大语料库上训练序列模型来预测下一个词元。 这些语料的构成可能各不相同，但主要是新闻、书籍、Github 代码，并混入少量从论坛抓取的数据（例如来自 Reddit、Stack Exchange 的数据），其中可能包含类似对话的数据。

sents.en: (1) Pretraining: a sequence model is trained to predict the next token on a gigantic corpus of mixed internet texts.
sents.zh: (1) 预训练：在一个由混合互联网文本组成的超大语料库上训练序列模型来预测下一个词元。

sents.en: The compositions may vary but they are predominantly news, books, Github code, with a small blend of forum-crawled data such as from Reddit, Stack Exchange, which may contain dialogue-like data.
sents.zh: 这些语料的构成可能各不相同，但主要是新闻、书籍、Github 代码，并混入少量从论坛抓取的数据（例如来自 Reddit、Stack Exchange 的数据），其中可能包含类似对话的数据。

paragraphs.en: (2) Introduce dialogue formatting: because the sequence model only processes strings, while the most natural representation of dialogue history is a structured index of system prompts and past exchanges, a certain kind of formatting must be introduced for the purpose of conversion. Some Huggingface tokenizers provide this method called tokenizer.apply_chat_template for the convenience of users. The exact formatting differs from model to model, but it usually involves guarding the system prompts with <system> or <INST> in the hope that the pretrained model could allocate more attention weights to them. The system prompt plays a significant role in adapting language models to downstream applications and ensuring its safe behavior (we will talk more in the next section). Notably, the choice of the format is arbitrary at this step—pretraining corpus doesn’t follow this format.
paragraphs.zh: (2) 引入对话格式化：由于序列模型只处理字符串，而对话历史最自然的表示形式是系统提示与历史交互的结构化索引，因此必须为转换目的引入某种格式化方式。 一些 Huggingface 分词器提供了名为 tokenizer.apply_chat_template 的方法，以方便用户使用。 具体格式因模型而异，但通常会用 <system> 或 <INST> 来包裹系统提示，希望预训练模型能为它们分配更多的注意力权重。 系统提示在使语言模型适配下游应用以及确保其行为安全方面发挥着重要作用（我们将在下一节详细讨论）。 值得注意的是，这一步对格式的选择是任意的——预训练语料并不遵循这种格式。

paragraphs.en: (3) RLHF: In this step, the chatbot is directly rewarded or penalized for generating desired or undesired answers. It’s worth noting that this is the first time the introduced dialogue formatting appears in the training data. RLHF is a fine -tuning step not only because the data size is dwarfed in comparison to the pretraining corpus, but also due to the KL penalty and targeted weight tuning (e.g. Lora). Using Lecun’s analogy of cake baking, RLHF is only the small cherry on the top.
paragraphs.zh: (3) RLHF：在此步骤中，聊天机器人会因生成期望或不期望的回答而直接获得奖励或惩罚。 值得注意的是，这是所引入的对话格式首次出现在训练数据中。 RLHF 之所以是一个微调步骤，不仅是因为其数据量相较于预训练语料库相形见绌，还因为 KL 惩罚以及有针对性的权重调整（例如 Lora）。 用 Lecun 的蛋糕烘焙类比来说，RLHF 只是蛋糕顶上的那一颗小樱桃。

sents.zh: (3) RLHF：在此步骤中，聊天机器人会因生成期望或不期望的回答而直接获得奖励或惩罚。

paragraphs.en: Currently, “system prompt” is the main method that allows users to control LM behavior. However, researchers found evidence that LLMs can be brittle in following these instructions under adversarial conditions [12,13]. Readers might also have experienced this through daily interactions with ChatGPT or Claude—when a new chat window is freshly opened, the model can follow your instruction reasonably well [2], but after several rounds of dialogue, it’s no longer fresh , even stops following its role altogether.
paragraphs.zh: 目前，“系统提示词”是让用户控制语言模型行为的主要方法。 然而，研究人员发现证据表明，大语言模型在对抗性条件下遵循这些指令时可能表现得脆弱 [12,13]。 读者可能在与 ChatGPT 或 Claude 的日常交互中也经历过这种情况——当新聊天窗口刚打开时，模型能较好地遵循你的指令 [2]，但经过几轮对话后，它就不再“新鲜”，甚至完全不再遵循其角色设定。

paragraphs.en: How could we quantitatively capture this anecdote? For one-round instruction following, we’ve already enjoyed plenty of benchmarks such as MT-Bench and Alpaca-Eval. However, when we test models in an interactive fashion, it’s hard to anticipate what the model generates and prepare a reply in advance. In a project by my collaborators and me [3], we built an environment to synthesize dialogues with unlimited length to stress-test the instruction-following capabilities of LLM chatbots.
paragraphs.zh: 我们如何定量地捕捉这个轶事？ 对于单轮指令遵循，我们已经有很多基准可用，例如 MT-Bench 和 Alpaca-Eval。 然而，当我们以交互方式测试模型时，很难预测模型会生成什么并提前准备好回复。 在我和我的合作者的一个项目 [3] 中，我们构建了一个环境来合成长度不受限制的对话，以对 LLM 聊天机器人的指令遵循能力进行压力测试。

paragraphs.en: To allow an unconstrained scaling on the time scale, we let two system-prompted LM agents chat with each other for an extended number of rounds. This forms the main trunk of dialogue [a1, b1, a2, b2, …, a8, b8] (say the dialogue is 8-round). At this point, we could probably figure out how the LLMs stick to its system prompts just by examining this dialogue, but many of the utterances can be irrelevant to the instructions, depending on where the conversation goes. Therefore, we hypothetically branch out at each round by asking a question directly related to the system prompts, and use a corresponding judging function to quantify how well it performs. All that's provided by the dataset is a bank of triplets of (system prompts, probe questions, and judging functions).
paragraphs.zh: 为了在时间尺度上实现不受限制的扩展，我们让两个由系统提示词驱动的语言模型智能体相互对话，持续多轮。 这构成了对话的主干 [a1, b1, a2, b2, …, a8, b8]（假设该对话为 8 轮）。 此时，仅通过检查这段对话，我们或许就能弄清楚大语言模型在多大程度上遵循其系统提示词，但很多话语可能与指令无关，这取决于对话的走向。 因此，我们假设性地在每一轮进行分支，提出一个与系统提示词直接相关的问题，并使用相应的评判函数来量化其表现好坏。 数据集所提供的只是一个由（系统提示词、探测问题和评判函数）三元组构成的库。

paragraphs.en: Averaging across scenarios and pairs of system prompts, we get a curve of instruction stability across rounds. To our surprise, the aggregated results on both LLaMA2-chat-70B and gpt-3.5-turbo-16k are alarming. Besides the added difficulty to prompt engineering, the lack of instruction stability also comes with safety concerns. When the chatbot drifts away from its system prompts that stipulate safety aspects, it becomes more susceptible to jailbreaking and prone to more hallucinations.
paragraphs.zh: 对各场景和多组系统提示进行平均后，我们得到了一条跨轮次的指令稳定性曲线。 令我们惊讶的是，在 LLaMA2-chat-70B 和 gpt-3.5-turbo-16k 上的汇总结果都令人担忧。 除了增加了提示工程的难度之外，指令稳定性的缺失还带来了安全性方面的隐忧。 当聊天机器人偏离规定安全事项的系统提示时，它就更容易被越狱攻击，也更容易产生更多幻觉。

paragraphs.en: The empirical results also contrast with the ever-increasing context length of LLMs. Theoretically, some long-context models can attend to a window of up to 100k tokens. However, in the dialogue setting, they become distracted after only 1.6k tokens (assuming each utterance is 100 tokens). In [3], we further theoretically showed how this is inevitable in a Transformer based LM chatbot under the current prompting scheme, and proposed a simple technique called split-softmax to mitigate such effects.
paragraphs.zh: 实证结果也与 LLM 不断增长的上下文长度形成对比。 从理论上讲，一些长上下文模型可以关注多达 10 万 token 的窗口。 然而，在对话设置中，仅处理 1.6k token 后它们就会分心（假设每条话语为 100 token）。 在 [3] 中，我们进一步从理论上证明了在当前提示方案下，基于 Transformer 的语言模型聊天机器人不可避免地会出现这种情况，并提出了一种称为 split-softmax 的简单技术来缓解这种影响。

paragraphs.en: One might ask at this point, why is it so bad? Why don't humans lose their persona just by talking to another person for 8 rounds? It’s arguable that human interactions are based on purposes and intentions [5] and these purposes precede the means rather than the opposite—LLM is fundamentally a fluent English generator, and the persona is merely a thin added layer.
paragraphs.zh: 有人可能会问，为什么情况会这么糟？ 为什么人类不会仅仅通过与另一个人交谈 8 轮就失去自己的人格？ 可以说，人类的互动建立在目的和意图之上 [5]，而且这些目的先于手段而非相反——LLM 本质上是一个流畅的英语生成器，而人格只是附加在上面的一层薄壳。

paragraphs.en: Pretraining? Pretraining endows the language model with the capability to model a distribution over internet personas as well as the lower-level language distribution of each persona [4]. However, even when one persona (or a mixture of a limited number of them) is specified by the instruction of system prompts, current approaches fail to single it out.
paragraphs.zh: 预训练？ 预训练赋予语言模型对互联网人格进行分布建模的能力，以及对每个人格的底层语言分布进行建模的能力 [4]。 然而，即使系统提示词的指令指定了某一个人格（或少数几个人格的混合），当前的方法也无法将其单独筛选出来。

paragraphs.en: RLHF? RLHF provides a powerful solution to adapting this multi-persona model to a “helpful and harmless assistant.” However, the original RLHF methods formulate reward maximization as a one-step bandit problem, and it is not generally possible to train with human feedback in the loop of conversation. (I’m aware of many advances in alignment but I want to discuss the original RLHF algorithm as a prototypical example.) This lack of multi-turn planning may cause models to suffer from task ambiguity [6] and learning superficial human-likeness rather than goal-directed social interaction [7].
paragraphs.zh: RLHF？ RLHF 为将这种多人设模型调整为“乐于助人且无害的助手”提供了强大的解决方案。然而，最初的 RLHF 方法将奖励最大化表述为单步老虎机问题，因此通常无法在对话回路中使用人类反馈进行训练。 （我知道对齐技术已有许多进展，但我想以最初的 RLHF 算法作为一个典型例子来讨论。）这种缺乏多轮规划的问题可能导致模型受到任务歧义的困扰 [6]，并且学到的是浮于表面的人类相似性，而非目标导向的社会互动 [7]。

paragraphs.en: Will adding more dialogue data in RLHF help? My guess is that it will, to a certain extent, but it will still fall short due to a lack of purpose. Sergey Levine pointed out in his blog that there is a fundamental difference between preference learning and intentions: “the key distinction is between viewing language generation as selecting goal-directed actions in a sequential process, versus a problem of producing outputs satisfying user preferences.”
paragraphs.zh: 在 RLHF 中加入更多对话数据会有帮助吗？ 我的猜测是，在一定程度上会有帮助，但由于缺乏目的性，它仍然会有不足。 Sergey Levine 在他的博客中指出，偏好学习与意图之间存在根本区别：“关键区别在于，是把语言生成视为在一个序列过程中选择有目标导向的动作，还是把它看作一个生成满足用户偏好的输出的问题。”

paragraphs.en: The problem of long-horizon planning has attracted some attention in the LLM community. For example, “decision-oriented dialogue” is proposed as a general class of tasks [8], where the AI assistant collaborates with humans to help them make complicated decisions, such as planning itineraries in a city and negotiating travel plans among friends. Another example, Sotopia [10], is a comprehensive social simulation platform that compiles various goal-driven dialogue scenarios including collaboration, negotiation, and persuasion.
paragraphs.zh: 长时程规划问题已经在 LLM 社区引起了一些关注。 例如，「面向决策的对话」被提出作为一类通用任务 [8]，其中 AI 助手与人类协作，帮助他们做出复杂的决策，例如在城市中规划行程以及在朋友之间协商旅行计划。 另一个例子是 Sotopia [10]，这是一个综合性的社会模拟平台，汇集了包括协作、协商和说服在内的多种目标驱动对话场景。

paragraphs.en: To fill in this gap, my collaborators and I propose a lightweight algorithm (Dialogue Action Tokens, DAT [11]) that guides an LM chatbot through a multi-round goal-driven dialogue. As shown in the image below, in each round of conversations, the dialogue history’s last token embedding is used as the input (state) to a planner (actor) which predicts several prefix tokens (actions) to control the generation process. By training the planner with a relatively stable RL algorithm TD3+BC, we show significant improvement over baselines on Sotopia, even surpassing the social capability scores of GPT-4.

paragraphs.en: The following are two research questions that I’m mostly excited about:
paragraphs.zh: 以下是我最感兴趣的两个研究问题：

paragraphs.en: (1) Better monitoring and control of dialogue systems with steering techniques. For example, the recently proposed TalkTurner (Chen et al.) adds a dashboard (Viégas et al) to open-sourced LLMs, enabling users to see and control how LLM thinks of themselves. Many weaknesses of current steering techniques are revealed and call for better solutions. For example, using activation steering to control two attributes (e.g., age and education level) simultaneously has been found to be difficult and can cause more language degradation. Another intriguing question is how to differentiate between LLM’s internal model of itself and that of the user. Anecdotally, chatting with Golden Gate Bridge Claude has shown that steering on the specific Golden Gate Bridge feature found by SAE sometimes causes Claude to think of itself as the San Francisco landmark, sometimes the users as the bridge, and other times the topic as such.
paragraphs.zh: （1）通过引导技术更好地监控和控制对话系统。 例如，最近提出的TalkTurner（Chen等人）为开源大语言模型添加了一个仪表盘（Viégas等人），使用户能够查看并控制大语言模型如何看待自己。 当前引导技术的许多弱点已经显现，亟需更好的解决方案。 例如，使用激活引导同时控制两个属性（如年龄和教育水平）已被发现十分困难，并可能导致更严重的语言退化。 另一个有趣的问题是如何区分大语言模型对自身的内部模型与其对用户的内部模型。 有趣的是，与金门大桥Claude的对话表明，基于稀疏自编码器（SAE）发现的金门大桥特定特征进行引导，有时会使Claude把自己看作那个旧金山地标，有时把用户看作那座桥，还有时把话题本身看作如此。

paragraphs.en: (2) Better utilization of off-line reward signals. In the case of set-up environments like Sotopia and “decision-oriented dialogues”, rewards signals are engineered beforehand. In the real world, users won’t leave numerical feedback of how they feel satisfied. However, there might be other clues in language (e.g., “Thanks!”, “That’s very helpful!”) or from external resources (e.g., users buying the product for a salesman AI, users move to a subsequent coding question for copilot within a short time frame). Inferring and utilizing such hidden reward signals could strengthen the network effect of online chatbots: good model → more users → learning from interacting with users → better model.
paragraphs.zh: (2) 更好地利用离线奖励信号。 在像 Sotopia 这样预先搭建的环境以及「面向决策的对话」中，奖励信号是事先设计好的。 在现实世界中，用户不会留下表示他们满意程度的数值反馈。 然而，语言中可能存在其他线索（例如「谢谢！」「这非常有帮助！」），或者来自外部资源的线索（例如用户购买了销售智能体推销的产品，用户在短时间内向编程助手提出下一个编程问题）。 推断并利用这类隐藏的奖励信号可以增强在线聊天机器人的网络效应：好的模型 → 更多用户 → 从与用户的交互中学习 → 更好的模型。
